memories.content: On 2026-07-16 Mara took her mother to a cardiology appointment at Reddington Hospital on Lagos Island and, reading the charts as a nurse, found the care excellent.

entities.name: Reddington Hospital
entities.description: Lagos hospital where Mara's mother is treated for atrial fibrillation

memories.content: Mara judged (2026-07-16) that she had been wrong to assume Canadian healthcare is simply better than Nigerian healthcare; basis: watching Reddington's cardiologist manage her mother's afib cleanly and unhurried in a way she never gets at the General.

Dr. Tunde Adeyemi, the family-friend doctor, joined the 2026-07-16 appointment and walked the cardiologist's plan through with Mara's mother in Yoruba so she understood it; Mara called it care you can't bill for.

entities.name: Dr. Tunde Adeyemi
entities.description: family-friend doctor who looks in on Mara's mother; distinct from uncle Tunde Bakare

memories.content: Chidi holds the view (relayed 2026-07-16) that their mother should move in with him permanently and not live alone; their mother refuses on principle, an old recurring family argument.
Mara reflected (2026-07-16) that she wished she could bring the gentleness she saw in her mother's Lagos care back to her own ICU work.
On 2026-07-16 Mara could not switch off her nurse instincts at her mother's appointment, reading every chart over the cardiologist's shoulder and asking many questions.
Mara judged (2026-07-16) the Reddington cardiologist to be sharp and unhurried in a way she never experiences at the General; basis: observing him manage her mother's afib in person.
